chunks: Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim al-Bajalī narrated from Ṣabbāḥ al-Ḥadhdhā’, who said:
I heard Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام saying:

“If a man among you, when he intends to travel, stands at the door of his house facing the direction toward which he is heading, then recites Fātiḥat al-Kitāb in front of him, to his right, and to his left, and Āyat al-Kursī in front of him, to his right, and to his left, then says: ‘O Allah, protect me and protect what is with me; keep me safe and keep safe what is with me; convey me and convey what is with me with Your good conveyance,’ Allah will protect him and protect what is with him, keep him safe and keep safe what is with him, and convey him and convey what is with him.”

He said: Then he said, “O Ṣabbāḥ, have you not seen a man being protected while what is with him is not protected, and remaining safe while what is with him does not remain safe, and arriving while what is with him does not arrive?” I said: “Yes, may I be your ransom.”

key_terms.آيَةَ الْكُرْسِيِّ: Āyat al-Kursī, recited here for divine safeguarding
key_terms.اللَّهُمَّ: O Allah; opening of direct supplication
key_terms.بَلِّغْنِي: cause me to reach my destination
key_terms.فَاتِحَةَ الْكِتَابِ: Sūrat al-Fātiḥah, recited here for blessing and protection

ai.seo_question: What supplication should be recited when leaving for travel for protection and safety?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches a recommended supplication and recitation for one setting out on travel. It emphasizes seeking Allah’s protection, safety, and successful arrival not only for the traveler but also for the possessions and things accompanying him.
